arxiv-1804-08501.title: Dropping Networks For Transfer Learning
arxiv-1804-08501.creator: James O’ Neill, Danushka Bollegala
arxiv-1804-08501.description: Abstract Many tasks in natural language understanding require learning relationships between two sequences for various tasks such as natural language inference, paraphrasing and entailment. These aforementioned tasks are similar in nature, yet they are often modeled individually. Knowledge transfer can be effective for closely related tasks.

arxiv-2111-13994.title: Bressoud’s identities for even moduli. New companions and related positivity results.
arxiv-2111-13994.creator: Alexander Berkovich
arxiv-2111-13994.description: Abstract . We revisit Bressoud’s generalised Borwein conjecture. Making use of certain positivity-preserving transformations for q q -binomial coefficients, we establish the truth of infinitely many new cases of the Bressoud conjecture. In addition, we prove new doubly-bounded refinement of the Foda-Quano identities. Finally, we discuss new companions to the Bressoud even moduli identities.

arxiv-2402-18770.description: Abstract In [ GORS14 ] , the HOMFLY polynomial of the ( m , n ) (m,n) torus knot T m , n T_{m,n} is extracted from the doubly graded character of the finite-dimensional representation L m n \mathrm{L}_{\frac{m}{n}} of the type A n − 1 A_{n-1} rational Cherednik algebra. It is furthermore conjectured in loc. cit.

arxiv-2501-17867.title: Low-Thrust Many-Revolution Trajectory Design Under Operational Uncertainties for DESTINY + Mission
arxiv-2501-17867.creator: Naoya Ozaki, Yuki Akiyama, Akira Hatakeyama, Shota Ito, Takuya Chikazawa, and Takayuki Yamamoto
arxiv-2501-17867.description: Abstract DESTINY + is a planned JAXA medium-class Epsilon mission from Earth to deep space using a low-thrust, many-revolution orbit. Such a trajectory design is a challenging problem not only for trajectory design but also for flight operations, and in particular, it is essential to evaluate the impact of operational uncertainties to ensure mission success.

pmc-11375896.title: Shape-Specific Gold Nanoparticles for Multiplex Biosensing Applications
pmc-11375896.creator: Shixi Zhang, Yuhan Zhang, Jiaye Jiang, Mathias Charconnet, Yuan Peng, Lei Zhang, Charles H. Lawrie
pmc-11375896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The biosensing field faces a significant challenge in efficiently detecting multiple analytes in a single diagnostic sample in order to compete with other established multiplex molecular diagnostic technologies such as PCR and ELISA. In response, we have developed a colorimetric nanobiosensor based on multiple morphological forms of functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) for the simultaneous detection of the influenza virus and SARS-CoV-2 virus.

pmc-11388773.title: Performance, interpersonal relationships and professional satisfaction: determinants to support pharmaceutical reengineering
pmc-11388773.creator: Fernando de Castro Araújo-Neto, Aline Santana Dosea, Divaldo Pereira de Lyra-Jr.
pmc-11388773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Professionalism represents the ethical contract that binds professionals and society. Its technical aspects, such as the professional practice model, form the foundation for attitudinal and behavioral characteristics, including the fiduciary relationship between pharmacists and patients. Despite significant interest in the topic, contextualizing professionalism proves to be a challenging endeavor, relying on collaboration among formal leaders, academics, and practitioners in the field.

pmc-11393834.title: Centriole Translational Planar Polarity in Monociliated Epithelia
pmc-11393834.creator: Antoine Donati, Sylvie Schneider-Maunoury, Christine Vesque, Rustem E Uzbekov
pmc-11393834.description: Ciliated epithelia are widespread in animals and play crucial roles in many developmental and physiological processes. Epithelia composed of multi-ciliated cells allow for directional fluid flow in the trachea, oviduct and brain cavities. Monociliated epithelia play crucial roles in vertebrate embryos, from the establishment of left–right asymmetry to the control of axis curvature via cerebrospinal flow motility in zebrafish.

pmc-11595926.title: Predicting Response to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Therapy in mCRPC Using Machine Learning
pmc-11595926.creator: Kaiyuan Gong, Baptiste Magnier, Salomé L’hostis, Fanny Borrely, Sébastien Le Bon, Nadine Houede, Adel Mamou, Laurent Maimoun, Pierre Olivier Kotzki, Vincent Boudousq, Dorota Bielińska-Wąż
pmc-11595926.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Radioligandtherapy (RLT) with [177Lu]Lu-PSMA has been newly introduced as a routine treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). However, not all patients can tolerate the entire therapeutic sequence, and in some cases, the treatment may prove ineffective. In real-world conditions, the aim is to distinguish between patients who fully benefit from treatment (those who respond effectively and tolerate the entire therapeutic sequence) and those who do not respond or cannot tolerate the entire sequence.

pmc-11608752.title: Risk factors of acute urinary retention after spine surgery
pmc-11608752.creator: Han-Hsi Chiu, Jui-Ming Liu, Kai-Jie Yu, Chun-Te Wu, See-Tong Pang, Po-Hung Lin
pmc-11608752.description: Acute postoperative urinary retention (APOUR) is 1 of the most common complications of spinal surgery, impacting both postoperative care and the patients’ quality of life. This study is designed to investigate the risk factors and the incidence of APOUR after spinal surgery in Taiwan.

pmc-12508466.title: Latent fingerprint recovery on submerged non-porous surfaces using phloxine B-based small particle reagent
pmc-12508466.creator: Dimpal Kushwaha, Jaisleen Kaur, Gurvinder Singh Sodhi
pmc-12508466.description: This study evaluates the effectiveness of a small particle reagent (SPR) formulation based on Phloxine B dye for developing latent fingerprints on submerged non-porous surfaces. The primary objectives were to assess the formulation’s ability to produce fingerprints over time and determine its shelf life.

pmc-12771907.title: The role of TGF-β1 C-509T and TGF-β1 T869C polymorphisms in susceptibility to tuberculosis infection in a Sudanese population: a case-control study
pmc-12771907.creator: Salma A. Moharrum, Naser Eldin Bilal, Najwa A. Mhmoud
pmc-12771907.description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) affects around 10 million people globally every year. The death rate from TB disease is substantial (almost 50%) if treatment is not received. In 2023, Sudan’s tuberculosis incidence is estimated at 134 cases per 100,000 population, with a 95% confidence interval of 125 to 145 cases per 100,000.

pmc-12971295.title: ‘SASADECC’—A Unique Model of Collaborative Care Between Government and Non‐Government Health Services for Adolescents With Complex Substance Use Issues
pmc-12971295.creator: David E. A. Gordon, Belinda Volkov, Arezu Akbarian, Lauren A. Monds, Mark Montebello
pmc-12971295.description: IntroductionDespite the importance of early intervention, major treatment gaps exist for adolescents with substance use issues. This report describes a unique collaboration between government and non‐government health services—The Specialist Addiction Service for Adolescents (SASA) adolescent addiction psychiatry service and Sydney Drug Education and Counselling Centre youth alcohol and other drug counselling service.

pmc-13199065.title: Heterogeneous causal mediation analysis using Bayesian additive regression trees
pmc-13199065.creator: Chen Liu, Xu Qin, Victor B Talisa, Jiebiao Wang
pmc-13199065.description: Causal mediation analysis provides insights into the mechanisms through which treatments affect outcomes. While mediation effects often vary across individuals, most existing methods focus solely on population-average effects, overlooking individual-level heterogeneity. To address this limitation, we propose a Bayesian regression tree ensemble method that flexibly models nonlinear relationships and captures treatment-by-mediator interactions in the mediation process.

pmc-13323075.creator: Jiarong Guo, Samuel T N Aroney, Guillermo Domínguez-Huerta, Derek Smith, Dean Vik, Carlos Owusu-Ansah, Akbar Adjie Pratama, Sergei Solonenko, Funing Tian, Cristina Howard-Varona, Zhi-Ping Zhong, Aminata Fofana, Garrett J Smith, Suzanne B Hodgkins, Dylan Cronin, IsoGenie Field Teams 2010–2017, 2019,
pmc-13323075.description: Ecosystems are shaped by communities of microorganisms whose niches and impacts depend on functional profiles influenced by gene gains and losses. pmc-13548625.title: Trajectories and associated factors of life-space in older patients following percutaneous coronary intervention: a mixed-methods study
pmc-13548625.creator: Yanyan Zhang, Bei Yang, Yin Wang, Kangyao Cheng
pmc-13548625.description: BackgroundOlder patients following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face long-term health risks such as in-stent restenosis. Life-space serves as a valuable clinical indicator for assessing and predicting the overall health of patients. Monitoring changes in life-space can facilitate early detection of health status changes.

pmc-13613444.title: Exploration of Metabolic Alterations in Methylmalonic Acidemia across Distinct Genetic Backgrounds
pmc-13613444.creator: Hai-Juan Zhi, Yi Ding, Yu-Xin Deng, Ting Chen, Yue Cao, Si-Yu Chang, Xia Zhan, Feng Xu, Li-Li Hao, Li-Li Liang, Wen-Juan Qiu, Hui-Wen Zhang, Xue-Fan Gu, Lian-Shu Han
pmc-13613444.description: Methylmalonic acidemia (MMA) is a rare recessively inherited disorder mainly caused by variants in the MMUT and MMACHC genes, leading to the accumulation of methylmalonic acid. The pathophysiological mechanisms of MMA remain poorly understood, and treatments are symptomatic. This study investigated the comprehensive metabolic remodeling signatures of the MMA subtypes.

pmc-13671448.title: Clinical manufacturing of adipose-derived stem cells for therapeutic use: current technologies, quality systems and production challenges
pmc-13671448.creator: Alexandre Asch, Daniel F Kalbermatten, Srinivas Madduri
pmc-13671448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThis systematic review evaluated manufacturing technologies for adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs), focusing on automation, quality control, potency, scalability, cost, and regulatory compliance.MethodsFollowing PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published January 2020–September 2025. Studies addressing clinical-grade ADSC manufacturing, quality control, regulatory compliance, or production economics were included; non-ADSC studies, reviews, case reports, and conference abstracts were excluded. Two reviewers qualitatively assessed methodological quality and bias.
